narration: Here is the whole framework in greyscale: a data preparation stage on the left, the training pipeline across the top, and the HOI restoration module along the bottom. We will bring it back to colour piece by piece.
First, the data preparation stage. This is where the training pairs for hand-object interaction video generation are built.
It starts from a reference frame. The object held in that frame is swapped for a new one, giving the object replacement image that defines the target appearance.
The resulting input frame is then annotated: box detection marks the hand and object regions, and hand mesh augmentation adds articulated hand geometry with motion cues.
Next, the training pipeline itself, which turns those prepared frames into generated video.
The reference image is encoded by a frozen VAE encoder and passed through the reference U-Net, whose self-attention layers capture the appearance to be preserved.
In parallel, the layout guidance frames go through the layout encoder and are added to sampled noise, forming the latent that will be denoised.
The denoising U-Net consumes that latent. Its blocks interleave self attention, temporal attention, and the new hand and object attention layers, with reference features injected from above.
A ControlNet branch encodes the hand mesh sequence and feeds the hand attention layers, so generated motion follows the intended articulation.
Zooming into the HOI restoration module: hand attention queries a hand texture memory bank through cross attention, and the result is gated by the hand mask before being merged back.
Object attention works the same way, reading an object texture memory bank and masking with the object mask, so object appearance stays faithful across frames.
Finally, the frozen VAE decoder turns the denoised latents into the generated frames, completing the pipeline now shown in full colour.
